objects.definition: typedef struct JSRuntime JSRuntime;
objects.description: Opaque runtime handle for the QuickJS engine. Owns global resources such as memory allocator, atoms table, job queue, and GC state. Must be created with JS_NewRuntime and freed with JS_FreeRuntime. Thread affinity applies for stack tracking.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSContext JSContext;
objects.description: Opaque execution context associated with a JSRuntime. Holds realm/global object, intrinsic objects, and per-context state. Create with JS_NewContext/JS_NewContextRaw and free with JS_FreeContext. Reference count style duplication via JS_DupContext.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSClass JSClass;
objects.description: Opaque internal class metadata structure used by QuickJS for object shapes. Only referenced; instances are managed internally. Not directly constructed by public API.
Header placed before ref-counted heap objects referenced by JSValue (strings, objects, symbols, bigints, etc.). Used to manage lifetime when duplicating/freeing JSValue. Not user-allocated directly.

Tagged JavaScript value representation (immediate integers/bools/tags and references to heap-managed objects). API functions create, convert, duplicate and free values. Users must call JS_FreeValue/JS_DupValue appropriately for ref-counted tags. Exact layout depends on build-time options (NaN-boxing or struct).
State passed to custom allocator callbacks tracking counts, sizes, and user opaque. Provided by QuickJS when using custom JSMallocFunctions.
Set of allocator callbacks used to create a runtime with JS_NewRuntime2. Enables embedding custom memory management and introspection.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSGCObjectHeader JSGCObjectHeader;
objects.description: Opaque header for GC-tracked objects used by the mark-and-sweep implementation. Exposed for custom mark functions but not defined here.
Aggregated memory usage statistics of a JSRuntime. Filled by JS_ComputeMemoryUsage and printable via JS_DumpMemoryUsage.
Descriptor for a property key during enumeration, carrying its atom and enumerability flag. Filled by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames and related APIs.
Property descriptor used by exotic methods/get_own_property and JS_GetOwnProperty. Holds flags and accessor/value fields.
Optional set of hooks to customize fundamental object internal methods for a class (Proxy-like or exotic behaviors). Typically referenced from JSClassDef.exotic.
Public class definition used to register a new class ID with JS_NewClass. Defines name, finalizer, GC marking, optional call behavior, and optional exotic methods.

objects.definition:
typedef enum JSTypedArrayEnum {
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_UINT8C = 0,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_INT8,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_UINT8,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_INT16,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_UINT16,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_INT32,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_UINT32,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_BIG_INT64,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_BIG_UINT64,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_FLOAT16,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_FLOAT32,
    JS_TYPED_ARRAY_FLOAT64,
} JSTypedArrayEnum;
objects.description: Enumeration of TypedArray element types supported by QuickJS. Used when creating typed arrays or querying their buffers.
Callbacks for host-managed SharedArrayBuffer backing stores. Install via JS_SetSharedArrayBufferFunctions to integrate with external SAB memory semantics.
States for Promise introspection, used by JS_PromiseState/JS_PromiseResult.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSModuleDef JSModuleDef;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a compiled/instantiated ES module inside QuickJS. Returned by module loader callbacks and used with module export/import APIs.
Union used to pass different C function pointer types into property/function definitions and JS_NewCFunction2. Selects behavior via JSCFunctionEnum.
Descriptor used to declaratively define properties, functions, accessors, constants, and nested objects on a JS object/class via JS_SetPropertyFunctionList.
Options controlling pretty-printing of JSValue for debugging/logging. Initialize with JS_PrintValueSetDefaultOptions and pass to JS_PrintValue/JS_PrintValueRT.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSAtom;
objects.description: Atom identifier for interned strings and symbols in QuickJS. Created and managed via JS_NewAtom/JS_DupAtom/JS_FreeAtom. Pointer form used as requested.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSClassID;
objects.description: Identifier for registered object classes in QuickJS. Allocate with JS_NewClassID and register with JS_NewClass.

/* in quickjs-libc.h */
/* forward from quickjs.h already included above */
objects.description: Same opaque module handle declared in quickjs.h; quickjs-libc.h only references it. No new definition here.

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new QuickJS runtime (global engine state). Use as the first step before creating any JSContext.
requirements: Must be paired with JS_FreeRuntime(rt) when no longer needed
Not thread-safe unless externally synchronized; use per-thread runtimes or ensure correct usage
Returned pointer must be non-NULL before use

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeInfo
functions.description: Associates an informational string with a runtime, typically for diagnostics or host labeling.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime* created by JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2
info must point to a NUL-terminated string whose lifetime exceeds that of rt (comment notes: info lifetime must exceed that of rt)

functions.name: JS_SetMemoryLimit
functions.description: Sets a soft memory limit (in bytes) for allocations done by the runtime to help control memory usage.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*
limit is in bytes; 0 may remove limit semantics depending on engine internals (not explicitly documented)

functions.name: JS_SetGCThreshold
functions.description: Sets the garbage collection trigger threshold (in bytes) for the runtime.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*

functions.name: JS_SetMaxStackSize
functions.description: Configures the maximum JS stack size checked by the engine; passing 0 disables the maximum stack size check.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*
Use 0 to disable maximum stack checks (as documented)

functions.name: JS_UpdateStackTop
functions.description: Updates internal record of the native stack top for the current thread for stack overflow checks when changing threads.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*
Must be called when changing threads that use the runtime (per comment)

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime2
functions.description: Creates a QuickJS runtime using a custom allocator and an opaque pointer saved in the runtime.
requirements: mf may be NULL or must point to a fully-initialized JSMallocFunctions with function pointers compliant with QuickJS expectations
opaque is stored and retrievable via JS_GetRuntimeOpaque

functions.name: JS_FreeRuntime
functions.description: Destroys a runtime, freeing all associated resources and invalidating any contexts created from it.
requirements: rt must be a runtime previously created by JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2
All JSContext objects created from rt must be freed before or by freeing the runtime (engine will clean up contexts but dangling external references are invalid afterward)
Do not use rt or any derived objects after call

functions.name: JS_GetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Retrieves the user-provided opaque pointer associated with the runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Sets an opaque host pointer on the runtime for later retrieval.

functions.name: JS_MarkValue
functions.description: Marks a JS value during GC marking using a host-provided callback to mark additional objects; used for embedding GC integration.
requirements: mark_func must be a valid function pointer when non-NULL

functions.name: JS_RunGC
functions.description: Forces a garbage collection cycle for the runtime.

functions.name: JS_IsLiveObject
functions.description: Returns non-zero if obj refers to a live (non-collected) object in the runtime.
requirements: obj should be a JS object value; behavior for non-objects is unspecified by header

functions.name: JS_NewContext
functions.description: Creates a new JS execution context bound to the given runtime, with all standard intrinsics enabled.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*
Check for NULL return before use

functions.name: JS_FreeContext
functions.description: Frees a JSContext and its resources.
requirements: s must be a context created by JS_NewContext/JS_NewContextRaw
Do not use s after calling
All JSValue references owned by the context should be released or will be cleaned up

functions.name: JS_DupContext
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a context and returns the same pointer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext*
Eventually pair with JS_FreeContext to balance references

functions.name: JS_GetContextOpaque
functions.description: Gets the user-defined opaque pointer stored on the context.

functions.name: JS_SetContextOpaque
functions.description: Sets an opaque host pointer on the context for user tracking.

functions.name: JS_GetRuntime
functions.description: Returns the runtime owning the given context.

functions.name: JS_SetClassProto
functions.signature: void JS_SetClassProto(JSContext *ctx, JSClassID class_id, JSValue obj);
functions.description: Associates a prototype object with a class ID in the context.
requirements: obj must be a JS object or null value; ownership of obj is transferred to the engine; follow JSValue reference-counting rules
class_id must be a valid registered class id

functions.name: JS_GetClassProto
functions.description: Retrieves the prototype object associated with a class ID in the context.
requirements: Returned JSValue follows reference-counting; must be freed with JS_FreeValue when no longer needed

functions.name: JS_NewContextRaw
functions.description: Creates a new minimal JSContext without adding intrinsic objects; caller must add desired intrinsics manually to save memory.
requirements: Add intrinsics via JS_AddIntrinsic* functions as needed

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects
functions.description: Adds base intrinsic objects (Object, Function, etc.) to a raw context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext* created typically by JS_NewContextRaw

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicDate
functions.description: Adds Date intrinsic to the context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicEval
functions.description: Adds eval-related intrinsics to the context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicStringNormalize
functions.description: Adds String normalization (Unicode) support intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExpCompiler
functions.description: Adds RegExp compiler intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExp
functions.description: Adds RegExp runtime intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicJSON
functions.description: Adds JSON intrinsics (JSON.parse/stringify).

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicProxy
functions.description: Adds Proxy intrinsic support.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicMapSet
functions.description: Adds Map and Set intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicTypedArrays
functions.description: Adds TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/DataView intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicPromise
functions.description: Adds Promise intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicWeakRef
functions.description: Adds WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry intrinsics.

functions.name: js_string_codePointRange
functions.signature: JSValue js_string_codePointRange(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Internal helper that likely implements a String method to get a range of code points. Intended for engine internals or module exposure.
requirements: ctx and this_val must be valid
argv must have at least argc entries

functions.name: js_malloc_rt
functions.description: Allocates memory using the runtime’s allocator.
requirements: size may be zero-treated per allocator semantics

functions.name: js_free_rt
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated with the runtime allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer obtained from js_malloc_rt/js_realloc_rt or compatible allocator of rt

functions.name: js_realloc_rt
functions.description: Reallocates memory using the runtime’s allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or previously allocated by the runtime allocator
size can be zero to free depending on allocator semantics

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size_rt
functions.description: Returns the usable size of an allocation from the runtime allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a valid allocation from the runtime allocator

functions.name: js_mallocz_rt
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory using the runtime allocator.

functions.name: js_malloc
functions.description: Allocates memory using the context’s allocator.

functions.name: js_free
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated with the context allocator.
requirements: ptr must be from js_malloc/js_realloc/js_mallocz for this context/runtime

functions.name: js_realloc
functions.description: Reallocates memory using the context’s allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or previously allocated by js_malloc/js_realloc
size may be zero per allocator semantics

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size
functions.description: Returns the usable allocation size from the context allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a valid allocation from the same allocator

functions.name: js_realloc2
functions.description: Reallocates memory and optionally returns slack/extra usable bytes in pslack.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or a pointer from the same allocator
pslack may be NULL or must point to writable size_t to receive slack

functions.name: js_mallocz
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory using the context allocator.

functions.name: js_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates a NUL-terminated C string using the context allocator.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: js_strndup
functions.description: Duplicates up to n bytes from a C string using the context allocator and NUL-terminates the copy.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer

functions.name: JS_ComputeMemoryUsage
functions.description: Fills a JSMemoryUsage structure with memory accounting information for the runtime.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable JSMemoryUsage

functions.name: JS_DumpMemoryUsage
functions.description: Writes a human-readable dump of the memory usage to a FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing
s must point to a valid JSMemoryUsage previously computed

functions.name: JS_NewAtomLen
functions.signature: JSAtom JS_NewAtomLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates or interns an atom from a byte string of exact length len.
requirements: str must point to at least len bytes (not necessarily NUL-terminated)

functions.name: JS_NewAtom
functions.description: Creates or interns an atom from a NUL-terminated C string.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: JS_NewAtomUInt32
functions.description: Creates or interns an atom representing a numeric property key (array index).

functions.name: JS_DupAtom
functions.description: Duplicates an atom (increments its refcount) and returns it.
requirements: v must be a valid atom obtained from QuickJS

functions.name: JS_FreeAtom
functions.description: Releases a reference to an atom for the context.
requirements: v must be a valid atom whose reference count you own

functions.name: JS_FreeAtomRT
functions.description: Releases a reference to an atom using a runtime-level API.
requirements: v must be a valid atom

functions.name: JS_AtomToValue
functions.description: Converts an atom to a JS string value.
requirements: Returned JSValue must be freed with JS_FreeValue when done

functions.name: JS_AtomToString
functions.description: Returns the string corresponding to an atom as a JSValue.

functions.name: JS_AtomToCStringLen
functions.description: Returns a C string pointer for the atom and optionally its byte length; the returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCString.
requirements: If plen != NULL, it must be writable
Caller must call JS_FreeCString(ctx, returned_ptr) when done

functions.name: JS_ValueToAtom
functions.description: Converts a JS value (string or symbol) to an atom.
requirements: val should be convertible to an atom (string/symbol) or may throw exception

functions.name: JS_NewClassID
functions.description: Allocates a new unique class ID, optionally storing it via pclass_id.
requirements: pclass_id may be NULL or must be writable

functions.name: JS_GetClassID
functions.description: Returns the class ID if v is an object; otherwise returns JS_INVALID_CLASS_ID.

functions.name: JS_NewClass
functions.signature: int JS_NewClass(JSRuntime *rt, JSClassID class_id, const JSClassDef *class_def);
functions.description: Registers a new class with the runtime using the given class definition.
requirements: class_id must have been allocated via JS_NewClassID
class_def must point to a fully populated JSClassDef that remains valid as required by engine (at least during registration)

functions.name: JS_IsRegisteredClass
functions.description: Returns non-zero if a class ID is registered in the runtime.

functions.name: JS_NewBigInt64
functions.description: Creates a BigInt JSValue from a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: Caller must free the returned value with JS_FreeValue when done

functions.name: JS_NewBigUint64
functions.description: Creates a BigInt (unsigned) JSValue from a 64-bit integer.
requirements: Caller must free the returned value with JS_FreeValue when done

functions.name: JS_Throw
functions.description: Throws a JS exception with the given error object and returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: obj must be an exception object or any JSValue; ownership is transferred to engine
After throwing, retrieve with JS_GetException if needed

functions.name: JS_SetUncatchableException
functions.description: Marks the current pending exception as uncatchable (if flag is TRUE) preventing it from being caught by JS code.
requirements: There must be a pending exception for effect

functions.name: JS_GetException
functions.description: Retrieves and clears the current pending exception from the context.
requirements: Only call when JS_HasException(ctx) indicates a pending exception
Caller must free the returned value

functions.name: JS_HasException
functions.description: Returns non-zero if there is a pending exception in the context.

functions.name: JS_IsError
functions.description: Checks whether a JS value is an Error object.

functions.name: JS_NewError
functions.description: Creates a new generic Error object.
requirements: Caller must free returned value when done

functions.name: JS_ThrowSyntaxError
functions.description: Formats and throws a SyntaxError with printf-style formatting; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string with matching variadic arguments

functions.name: JS_ThrowTypeError
functions.description: Formats and throws a TypeError; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt must be valid with matching args

functions.name: JS_ThrowReferenceError
functions.description: Formats and throws a ReferenceError; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt must be valid with matching args

functions.name: JS_ThrowRangeError
functions.description: Formats and throws a RangeError; returns JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_ThrowInternalError
functions.description: Formats and throws an InternalError; returns JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_ThrowOutOfMemory
functions.description: Throws an Out of Memory exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: __JS_FreeValue
functions.description: Internal function to free a JSValue with refcount reaching zero.
requirements: v must be a valid value with refcount semantics

functions.name: __JS_FreeValueRT
functions.description: Internal function to free a JSValue at runtime level when its refcount reaches zero.
requirements: v must be a valid value

functions.name: JS_StrictEq
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_StrictEq(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Implements JavaScript strict equality (===) between two values.

functions.name: JS_SameValue
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SameValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Implements the ECMAScript SameValue comparison semantics.

functions.name: JS_SameValueZero
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SameValueZero(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Implements SameValueZero comparison (like Map/Set, treats +0 and -0 as equal).

functions.name: JS_ToBool
functions.description: Converts a JS value to boolean; returns -1 on exception, otherwise 0 or 1.

functions.name: JS_ToInt32
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a 32-bit signed integer; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: pres must be a writable pointer

functions.name: JS_ToInt64
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a 64-bit signed integer; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToIndex
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a valid array index (uint64); returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToFloat64
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a double; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToBigInt64
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a signed 64-bit integer; returns exception if val is a Number; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: Per comment: returns an exception if 'val' is a Number

functions.name: JS_ToInt64Ext
functions.description: Converts a JS value to int64, allowing BigInt; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_NewStringLen
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewStringLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str1, size_t len1);
functions.description: Creates a new JS string from a byte buffer of length len1.
requirements: str1 must point to at least len1 bytes (not necessarily NUL-terminated)
Caller must free returned value when done

functions.name: JS_NewAtomString
functions.description: Creates a JS string that is also interned as an atom.

functions.name: JS_ToString
functions.description: Converts a value to a JS string; may throw; returns JS_EXCEPTION on error.

functions.name: JS_ToPropertyKey
functions.description: Converts a value to a valid property key (string or symbol).

functions.name: JS_ToCStringLen2
functions.signature: const char *JS_ToCStringLen2(JSContext *ctx, size_t *plen, JSValueConst val1, JS_BOOL cesu8);
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated C string representation of a JS value, optionally in CESU-8, with length via plen; must be freed with JS_FreeCString.
requirements: If plen != NULL it must be writable

functions.name: JS_FreeCString
functions.description: Frees a C string previously obtained from JS_ToCString/JS_AtomToCString.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by a QuickJS C-string API for this context/runtime

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProtoClass
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewObjectProtoClass(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst proto, JSClassID class_id);
functions.description: Creates a new object with an explicit prototype and class ID.
requirements: proto must be an object or null prototype value
class_id must be a registered class

functions.name: JS_NewObjectClass
functions.description: Creates a new object with the given class ID and default prototype for that class.
requirements: class_id must be a registered class

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProto
functions.description: Creates a new plain object with a specified prototype.
requirements: proto must be an object or null

functions.name: JS_NewObject
functions.description: Creates a new plain object with the default Object prototype.

functions.name: JS_IsFunction
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is a function object.

functions.name: JS_IsConstructor
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is a constructor function (can be called with new).

functions.name: JS_SetConstructorBit
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SetConstructorBit(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JS_BOOL val);
functions.description: Sets or clears the internal constructor bit of a function object, controlling whether it can be used as a constructor.
requirements: func_obj must be a function object

functions.name: JS_NewArray
functions.description: Creates a new Array object.

functions.name: JS_IsArray
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is an Array object; may throw for proxies.

functions.name: JS_NewDate
functions.description: Creates a new Date object from milliseconds since Unix epoch.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyInternal
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyInternal(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, JSValueConst receiver, JS_BOOL throw_ref_error);
functions.description: Low-level property get with explicit receiver and option to throw on undefined reference errors.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must free non-exception values

functions.name: JS_GetProperty
functions.signature: static js_force_inline JSValue JS_GetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for JS_GetPropertyInternal using this_obj as receiver and no throw_ref_error.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom
Caller must free returned value unless exception

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop);
functions.description: Gets a property by C string name.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated string
Caller must free returned value unless exception

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx);
functions.description: Gets a property by 32-bit array index.
requirements: Caller must free returned value unless exception

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyInternal
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyInternal(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val, JSValueConst this_obj, int flags);
functions.description: Low-level property set with explicit receiver and behavior flags; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.
requirements: Ownership of val may be consumed by the engine depending on success/flags; follow QuickJS conventions

functions.name: JS_SetProperty
functions.signature: static inline int JS_SetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Convenience setter that throws on failure (JS_PROP_THROW). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by 32-bit index. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyInt64
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyInt64(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, int64_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by 64-bit index. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyStr
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by C string name. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated string

functions.name: JS_HasProperty
functions.signature: int JS_HasProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Checks whether an object has a property; returns 1 if exists, 0 if not, -1 on exception.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom

functions.name: JS_IsExtensible
functions.description: Returns 1 if object is extensible, 0 if not, or -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_PreventExtensions
functions.description: Prevents new properties from being added to the object; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_DeleteProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DeleteProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, int flags);
functions.description: Deletes a property; behavior may depend on flags; returns 1 on success, 0 if not deleted, -1 on exception.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom

functions.name: JS_SetPrototype
functions.signature: int JS_SetPrototype(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst proto_val);
functions.description: Sets the prototype of obj to proto_val; returns 0 on success, -1 on exception or FALSE-equivalent per engine semantics.
requirements: proto_val must be an object or null

functions.name: JS_GetPrototype
functions.description: Gets the prototype of a value/object; returns a JSValue (object or null) or exception.

functions.name: JS_GetOwnPropertyNames
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnPropertyNames(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyEnum **ptab, uint32_t *plen, JSValueConst obj, int flags);
functions.description: Enumerates own property keys of obj according to flags; returns 0 on success or -1 on exception; results are written to ptab/plen.
requirements: ptab and plen must be non-NULL and writable
Caller must free the table with JS_FreePropertyEnum(ctx, *ptab, *plen)

functions.name: JS_FreePropertyEnum
functions.description: Frees an array returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames.
requirements: tab must be the pointer returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames
len must match the length returned

functions.name: JS_GetOwnProperty
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyDescriptor *desc, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Retrieves an own property descriptor for a property if present; returns >=0 success flag, <0 on exception.
requirements: desc may be NULL or must be writable when non-NULL
prop must be a valid atom

functions.name: JS_Call
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Call(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst this_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Calls a JS function with given this and arguments.
requirements: argv must point to at least argc arguments
Caller must free returned value unless exception

functions.name: JS_Invoke
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Invoke(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, JSAtom atom, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Invokes a method by property atom name on this_val with arguments.
requirements: atom must be a valid property atom
argv must have at least argc items
Caller must free return value unless exception

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Invokes a constructor (new func_obj(...)).
requirements: argv must have at least argc items
Caller must free returned value unless exception

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor2(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst new_target, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Invokes a constructor with an explicit new.target value.
requirements: new_target must be a constructor function
argv must have at least argc items

functions.name: JS_DetectModule
functions.description: Heuristically detects if the given JS source is a module; input must be NUL-terminated per comment.
requirements: input must point to a buffer of length input_len and input[input_len] must be '\0' as documented

functions.name: JS_Eval
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Eval(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Compiles and optionally executes JavaScript source code in the given context; returns result or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: input must be a buffer of length input_len and be NUL-terminated at input[input_len] per comment
filename must be a NUL-terminated string for diagnostics (may be NULL)
eval_flags must be a combination of JS_EVAL_* constants

functions.name: JS_EvalThis
functions.signature: JSValue JS_EvalThis(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Same as JS_Eval but with an explicit this object.
requirements: this_obj should be an object or appropriate this binding
input buffer must be NUL-terminated at input[input_len]

functions.name: JS_GetGlobalObject
functions.description: Returns the global object of the context.
requirements: Caller must free returned value when done

functions.name: JS_IsInstanceOf
functions.signature: int JS_IsInstanceOf(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst obj);
functions.description: Implements val instanceof obj; returns 1 true, 0 false, -1 on exception.
requirements: obj should be a function with prototype or @@hasInstance

functions.name: JS_DefineProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DefineProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst getter, JSValueConst setter, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a property with attributes and optional accessor on an object; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure, -1 on exception.
requirements: Flags control presence of attributes (JS_PROP_HAS_* etc.)

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValue
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a data property with given value and flags.
requirements: Ownership of val may be transferred by engine

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a data property at a numeric index with flags.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueStr
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a data property by string name with flags.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyGetSet
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyGetSet(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue getter, JSValue setter, int flags);
functions.description: Defines an accessor property with getter and/or setter functions and flags.
requirements: getter/setter must be callable or undefined/null

functions.name: JS_SetOpaque
functions.description: Associates a host opaque pointer with an object of a registered class.
requirements: obj must be an object instance of a class supporting opaque payloads

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque
functions.description: Gets the opaque pointer from an object if it has the given class ID; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: class_id must match the object's class

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque2
functions.description: Like JS_GetOpaque but throws a TypeError if obj is not of the expected class.
requirements: obj should be an object of expected class

functions.name: JS_GetAnyOpaque
functions.description: Returns the opaque pointer and optionally the class ID for any object with an opaque payload.
requirements: class_id may be NULL or writable to receive the class id

functions.name: JS_ParseJSON
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ParseJSON(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len, const char *filename);
functions.description: Parses JSON text from a NUL-terminated buffer into a JS value; buffer must be NUL-terminated at buf[buf_len].
requirements: buf must be a buffer of length buf_len and buf[buf_len] == '\0'

functions.name: JS_ParseJSON2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ParseJSON2(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len, const char *filename, int flags);
functions.description: Parses JSON with optional extended features when flags include JS_PARSE_JSON_EXT.
requirements: buf must be NUL-terminated at buf[buf_len]

functions.name: JS_JSONStringify
functions.signature: JSValue JS_JSONStringify(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst replacer, JSValueConst space0);
functions.description: Serializes a value to JSON string, honoring replacer and spacing.

functions.name: JS_NewArrayBuffer
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayBuffer(JSContext *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t len, JSFreeArrayBufferDataFunc *free_func, void *opaque, JS_BOOL is_shared);
functions.description: Creates an ArrayBuffer wrapping an existing data buffer with a custom free callback and optional shared flag.
requirements: buf must point to len bytes and remain valid until free_func is called
free_func may be NULL only if engine takes ownership without callback (implementation-defined); otherwise must free buf using rt passed to callback

functions.name: JS_NewArrayBufferCopy
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayBufferCopy(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates a new ArrayBuffer by copying data from buf.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes

functions.name: JS_DetachArrayBuffer
functions.description: Detaches the ArrayBuffer, making its contents inaccessible.
requirements: obj must be an ArrayBuffer object

functions.name: JS_GetArrayBuffer
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the backing store of an ArrayBuffer and its size.
requirements: The returned pointer is valid as long as the buffer is not detached/freed

functions.name: JS_NewTypedArray
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewTypedArray(JSContext *ctx, int argc, JSValueConst *argv, JSTypedArrayEnum array_type);
functions.description: Creates a new TypedArray of the specified type based on arguments (constructor-like semantics).
requirements: argv must have at least argc entries
array_type must be a valid JSTypedArrayEnum value

functions.name: JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, size_t *pbyte_offset, size_t *pbyte_length, size_t *pbytes_per_element);
functions.description: Gets the underlying ArrayBuffer of a TypedArray, along with byte offset, length, and bytes per element.
requirements: Output pointers may be NULL or must be writable when non-NULL
Caller must free returned ArrayBuffer value

functions.name: JS_SetSharedArrayBufferFunctions
functions.description: Installs host callbacks for SharedArrayBuffer allocation, free, and duplicate operations.
requirements: sf must point to a structure with valid function pointers; persists as long as used by runtime

functions.name: JS_NewPromiseCapability
functions.description: Creates a new Promise and stores resolve/reject functions into resolving_funcs[0] and resolving_funcs[1].
requirements: resolving_funcs must point to storage for two JSValue items
Caller must free returned values appropriately

functions.name: JS_PromiseState
functions.description: Returns the current state of a JavaScript Promise associated with the given context. The return value is one of JSPromiseStateEnum: JS_PROMISE_PENDING, JS_PROMISE_FULFILLED, or JS_PROMISE_REJECTED. Typical usage: call this to check whether a Promise is settled; if settled, you can then call JS_PromiseResult() to obtain its fulfillment value or rejection reason. Behavior when passing a non-Promise value is not documented in this header and is unknown.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a JSContext.
promise should be a valid JSValue referring to a Promise object; behavior for non-Promise inputs is unspecified/unknown based on the header.
The JSValue should originate from the same JSRuntime as ctx (inferred from QuickJS API patterns).
The function does not take ownership of promise; the caller remains responsible for managing the value’s lifetime per QuickJS reference-counting rules (e.g., JS_DupValue/JS_FreeValue).
No error/exception reporting is documented for this function; callers should not rely on exceptions being thrown for invalid inputs (unknown behavior).

functions.name: JS_PromiseResult
functions.description: Returns the result or reason of a settled Promise.
requirements: promise should be settled; returns JS_EXCEPTION on misuse

functions.name: JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker
functions.description: Sets a host callback to be notified of unhandled Promise rejections and handling state changes.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear, otherwise must remain valid

functions.name: JS_SetInterruptHandler
functions.description: Registers a host callback polled by the engine to interrupt execution; returning non-zero from cb interrupts JS execution.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL must be thread-safe relative to runtime usage

functions.name: JS_SetCanBlock
functions.description: Informs the runtime whether Atomics.wait() can block in the host environment.

functions.name: JS_SetStripInfo
functions.description: Selects which debug/source info to strip from compiled code using JS_STRIP_* flags.
requirements: flags is a combination of JS_STRIP_SOURCE and/or JS_STRIP_DEBUG

functions.name: JS_GetStripInfo
functions.description: Returns the current strip info flags set on the runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetIsHTMLDDA
functions.description: Marks an object with the [IsHTMLDDA] internal slot (legacy web-compat behavior).

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc
functions.description: Installs module normalization and loading callbacks for import resolution. Attributes not supported with this variant.
requirements: module_normalize may be NULL to use default normalizer
module_loader must be non-NULL to enable custom loading or NULL to clear
opaque is passed back to callbacks

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2
functions.signature: void JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2(JSRuntime *rt, JSModuleNormalizeFunc *module_normalize, JSModuleLoaderFunc2 *module_loader, JSModuleCheckSupportedImportAttributes *module_check_attrs, void *opaque);
functions.description: Installs module loader callbacks with support for import attributes and attribute validation.
requirements: module_loader may be NULL to clear
module_check_attrs may be NULL to disable attribute checking

functions.name: JS_GetImportMeta
functions.description: Returns the import.meta object for a module.
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer

functions.name: JS_GetModuleName
functions.description: Returns the module’s name as an atom.
requirements: Caller should JS_FreeAtom(ctx, atom) when done if they dup it or per engine usage

functions.name: JS_GetModuleNamespace
functions.description: Returns the module namespace object for a module definition.

functions.name: JS_EnqueueJob
functions.signature: int JS_EnqueueJob(JSContext *ctx, JSJobFunc *job_func, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Enqueues a microtask/job to be executed by the job queue.
requirements: job_func must be a valid function pointer
argv must have at least argc entries if argc > 0

functions.name: JS_IsJobPending
functions.description: Returns non-zero if there are pending jobs in the runtime’s job queue.

functions.name: JS_ExecutePendingJob
functions.description: Executes one pending job; returns <0 on exception; pctx receives the context in which job ran.
requirements: pctx must be non-NULL and writable

functions.name: JS_WriteObject
functions.signature: uint8_t *JS_WriteObject(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags);
functions.description: Serializes a JS value/module/function into a binary blob; returns allocated buffer and its size in psize.
requirements: obj must be serializable under given flags
Caller must free returned buffer via js_free/js_free_rt per allocator

functions.name: JS_WriteObject2
functions.signature: uint8_t *JS_WriteObject2(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags, uint8_t ***psab_tab, size_t *psab_tab_len);
functions.description: Like JS_WriteObject but also collects SharedArrayBuffer references into psab_tab and length.
requirements: psab_tab and psab_tab_len may be NULL or must be writable when non-NULL
Caller must free returned buffers appropriately

functions.name: JS_ReadObject
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ReadObject(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_len, int flags);
functions.description: Deserializes a previously written object/function/module from a buffer; returns a JS value or exception.
requirements: buf must point to buf_len bytes
flags must allow expected object types

functions.name: JS_EvalFunction
functions.description: Instantiates and evaluates a compiled function or module object (e.g., result of JS_ReadObject).
requirements: fun_obj must be a compiled function/module object

functions.name: JS_ResolveModule
functions.description: Loads dependencies of a module returned by JS_ReadObject.
requirements: obj must be a module value

functions.name: JS_GetScriptOrModuleName
functions.description: Returns the script or module name for a given number of stack levels up; exported for os.Worker.

functions.name: JS_LoadModule
functions.signature: JSValue JS_LoadModule(JSContext *ctx, const char *basename, const char *filename);
functions.description: Loads a module given a base path and filename; exported for os.Worker.
requirements: basename and filename must be NUL-terminated strings

functions.name: JS_NewCFunction2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunction2(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunction *func, const char *name, int length, JSCFunctionEnum cproto, int magic);
functions.description: Creates a JS function object wrapping a C function with name, length, prototype, and optional magic value.
requirements: func must be a valid C callback matching cproto
name must be NUL-terminated or NULL

functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionData
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunctionData(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunctionData *func, int length, int magic, int data_len, JSValueConst *data);
functions.description: Creates a C function object with embedded data values accessible to the function.
requirements: func must be a valid C callback of type JSCFunctionData
If data_len > 0, data must point to at least data_len JSValueConst entries

functions.name: JS_NewCFunction
functions.signature: static inline JSValue JS_NewCFunction(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunction *func, const char *name, int length);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for JS_NewCFunction2 with JS_CFUNC_generic and magic=0.
requirements: func must be a valid JSCFunction*

functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionMagic
functions.signature: static inline JSValue JS_NewCFunctionMagic(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunctionMagic *func, const char *name, int length, JSCFunctionEnum cproto, int magic);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to create a C function using a magic-enabled callback and specified cproto and magic.
requirements: func must be valid and match cproto expectations

functions.name: JS_SetConstructor
functions.signature: void JS_SetConstructor(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst proto);
functions.description: Associates a constructor function with its prototype object (sets function.prototype and prototype.constructor appropriately).
requirements: func_obj must be a function object

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyFunctionList
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyFunctionList(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, const JSCFunctionListEntry *tab, int len);
functions.description: Defines a list of properties (functions, constants, accessors, etc.) on an object from a static table.
requirements: tab must point to an array of length len

functions.name: JS_NewCModule
functions.description: Creates a new C-defined module with the given name and an initialization callback.
requirements: func must be a valid initializer which defines exports

functions.name: JS_AddModuleExport
functions.description: Declares an export name for a C module before instantiation.
requirements: m must be a module created by JS_NewCModule
Must be called before module is instantiated (as documented)

functions.name: JS_AddModuleExportList
functions.signature: int JS_AddModuleExportList(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m, const JSCFunctionListEntry *tab, int len);
functions.description: Declares multiple exports for a C module from a function list table, before instantiation.
requirements: m must be a C module and not yet instantiated
tab must be non-NULL with at least len entries

functions.name: JS_SetModuleExport
functions.signature: int JS_SetModuleExport(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m, const char *export_name, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets the value of an export on a C module after instantiation.

requirements: tab must have at least len entries

functions.name: JS_SetModulePrivateValue
functions.description: Associates a JSValue private payload with a C module.
requirements: Ownership of val may be transferred

functions.name: JS_GetModulePrivateValue
functions.description: Retrieves the module’s private JSValue payload.

functions.name: JS_PrintValueSetDefaultOptions

functions.signature: void js_std_promise_rejection_tracker(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst promise, JSValueConst reason, JS_BOOL is_handled, void *opaque);

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator targets fuzzing stubs that primarily consume arbitrary byte strings via
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR(). Those strings are then fed to QuickJS APIs such as:
# - JS_NewStringLen (expects arbitrary bytes, not necessarily UTF-8)
# - JS_NewAtomLen (arbitrary bytes of exact length)
# - Various conversions (ToInt/ToFloat/ToIndex/ToBigInt64) where providing strings that look
#   like numbers, hex, bigint literals, whitespace variants, Unicode digits, etc., will
#   exercise different coercion paths.
# - ArrayBuffer copy and typed array paths where arbitrary binary payloads of different sizes
#   are interesting (including zero-length, powers of two, typical sizes, and text vs. binary).
# - JSON-related helpers where valid JSON texts as well as edge JSON values increase coverage.
# - Property/atom names: identifiers, Unicode escapes, long names, empty names, numeric keys.
#
# Strategy
# - Produce a single byte-string that concatenates multiple self-delimited segments.
# - Each call to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in the fuzzer will draw from this buffer in order; providing a
#   rich mix increases the chance each stub sees meaningful inputs.
# - We use a simple TLV framing: [count][segments...], where each segment is [len32][bytes].
#   The fuzzer infrastructure commonly slices sequentially; a TLV stream ensures each segment is
#   individually valid regardless of internal NULs.
# - Segment palette includes: numbers in various radices, JSON snippets, UTF-8 with edge code
#   points, CESU-8-like surrogate pairs, long/short strings, purely binary blocks, property-like
#   names, and empty strings. Total size limited to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii_ident(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> bytes:
    first_chars = "$_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    rest_chars = first_chars + "0123456789"
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    s = rng.choice(first_chars)
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s.encode('ascii', 'strict')

def _rand_utf8_text(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> bytes:
    # Include a range of code points, including edge cases and combining marks
    pieces = []
    base_pool = [
        "", "a", "A", "å", "é", "Ω", "Ж", "你", "𐍈",  # BMP + non-BMP
        "𝒜", "😀", "🏳️‍🌈",  # emoji and ZWJ sequences
        "e01",  # e + combining acute
        "\u200d", "\u200b",  # ZWJ / ZWSP
    ]
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    while sum(len(p.encode('utf-8')) for p in pieces) < length:
        pieces.append(rng.choice(base_pool))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            pieces.append(chr(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E)))
    s = ''.join(pieces)
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    return b[:max_len]

def _rand_binary(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    # Mix patterns: zeroes, 0xff, incrementing, random
    choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if choice == 0:
        return bytes([0]) * n
    elif choice == 1:
        return bytes([0xFF]) * n
    elif choice == 2:
        return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n)))
    else:
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _number_like_strings(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    vals = []
    # Integers and floats in multiple formats
    ints = [
        "0", "-0", "1", "-1", "42", "-2147483648", "2147483647",
        str(rng.randint(-2**63, 2**63 - 1)),
    ]
    floats = [
        "0.0", "-0.0", "3.14159", "-1e10", "1e-10", "NaN", "Infinity", "+Infinity", "-Infinity",
        f"{rng.uniform(-1e308,1e308):.17g}",
    ]
    hexes = ["0x0", "0x7fffffff", "-0x80000000", hex(rng.getrandbits(64))]
    bigints = ["0n", "1n", "-1n", f"{rng.randint(-10**18,10**18)}n"]
    whites = [" \t\n42", "\n\r\t-7 ", "\u00a0\t123"]
    for s in ints + floats + hexes + bigints + whites:
        vals.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
    return vals

def _json_snippets(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    samples = [
        b"null", b"true", b"false", b"0", b"[]", b"{}",
        b"{\"a\":1}", b"[1,2,3]", b"{\"nested\":[{\"x\":\"y\"}]}",
    ]
    # Random small JSON object
    obj = { "a": rng.randint(-5,5), "b": rng.choice([True, False, None, "str"]) }
    try:
        import json
        samples.append(json.dumps(obj).encode('utf-8'))
    except Exception:
        pass
    return samples

def _property_name_variants(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    names = [
        b"", b"a", b"_", b"$", b"toString", b"constructor", b"__proto__",
        b"length", b"prototype", b"value", b"get", b"set",
        _rand_ascii_ident(rng, 24),
        _rand_utf8_text(rng, 32),
        str(rng.randint(0, 1000000)).encode('ascii'),
    ]
    # Include some with dots or unicode escapes-like content (as raw bytes)
    names.append(b"foo.bar")
    names.append(b"\xF0\x9F\x98\x80")  # UTF-8 for 😀
    return names

def _arraybuffer_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024]
    out = []
    for sz in rng.sample(sizes, k=min(len(sizes), 10)):
        block = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(sz))
        out.append(block)
    return out

def _dedupe_and_trim(segments: list[bytes], rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    # Remove duplicates while preserving order; trim overly large segments
    seen = set()
    result = []
    for s in segments:
        key = zlib.crc32(s)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        if len(s) > 1024:
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                s = s[:1024]
            else:
                # keep tail sometimes (useful for NUL-prefixed cases)
                s = s[-1024:]
        result.append(s)
    return result

def _pack_tlv(segments: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Format: [u16 count][ [u32 len][bytes] * count ]
    buf = bytearray()
    count = min(len(segments), 65535)
    buf += struct.pack('>H', count)
    for s in segments[:count]:
        buf += struct.pack('>I', len(s))
        buf += s
    return bytes(buf)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segments: list[bytes] = []

    # Ensure a mix of very short to moderate strings first (some stubs take first few FUZZ_PARAM_STRs)
    segments.extend([
        b"", b"0", b"1", b"-1", b"NaN", b"Infinity", b"true", b"false",
        b"{}", b"[]", b"null", b"k", b"v", b"name", b"value",
    ])

    # Numbers and coercion-friendly strings
    segments.extend(_number_like_strings(rng))

    # JSON snippets
    segments.extend(_json_snippets(rng))

    # Property names and atoms
    segments.extend(_property_name_variants(rng))

    # UTF-8 texts including complex cases
    for _ in range(6):
        segments.append(_rand_utf8_text(rng, rng.randint(0, 80)))

    # Binary payloads for ArrayBuffer copy and atom/string raw creation
    for _ in range(6):
        segments.append(_rand_binary(rng, rng.randint(0, 256)))

    # Deterministic patterned buffers and sizes interesting to typed arrays
    segments.extend(_arraybuffer_payloads(rng))

    # Additional edge-case strings for conversions and property APIs
    extra = [
        b"   42   ", b"\t-7\n", b"0xDEADBEEF", b"0755", b"0b101010",
        b"1_000_000",  # JS numeric literal with underscores (string input for ToNumber)
        b"\x00\x00",  # embedded NULs
        b"a\x00b\x00c",  # NUL-separated
        b"\xF4\x8F\xBF\xBF",  # U+10FFFF UTF-8
        b"\xED\xA0\x80\xED\xB0\x80",  # UTF-16 surrogate halves bytes (ill-formed UTF-8 but allowed as bytes)
    ]
    segments.extend(extra)

    # Long text to exercise string paths but capped to avoid large allocations
    long_text = ("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. " * 10).encode('utf-8')
    segments.append(long_text[:800])

    # Dedupe and trim segments
    segments = _dedupe_and_trim(segments, rng)

    # Shuffle order but keep some critical early ones at the front to seed valid cases
    head = segments[:12]
    tail = segments[12:]
    rng.shuffle(tail)
    segments = head + tail

    # Pack into TLV until size limit
    out = bytearray()
    packed = []
    total_overhead = 2  # u16 count
    remaining = MAX_TOTAL - total_overhead
    for s in segments:
        need = 4 + len(s)  # u32 len + payload
        if need > remaining:
            # Try truncating large s if possible
            if remaining > 4:
                trunc_len = remaining - 4
                if trunc_len > 0:
                    packed.append(s[:trunc_len])
                    remaining = 0
            break
        packed.append(s)
        remaining -= need

    return _pack_tlv(packed)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: NUL-terminated C string
# The fuzzer stubs consume std::string via FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), which provides
# a NUL-terminated buffer when accessed with c_str(). Our generator should
# therefore return byte sequences that, when used as the fuzzable buffer,
# are interesting but valid C strings (include a terminating NUL at the end),
# and remain within 4096 bytes.
#
# Stubs covered and considerations:
# - js_strdup/js_strndup: any NUL-terminated string. Include empty, short, long, and
#   strings with embedded NUL not possible here because std::string stores data bytes
#   and c_str() adds a NUL terminator; embedded NULs can be included in the byte buffer
#   but most C APIs treat them as terminators. For variety, we can include internal NULs;
#   js_strndup respects length n separate from the terminating NUL in input.
# - Atom APIs (JS_NewAtom, JS_NewAtomLen indirectly via NewAtom using c_str()): valid
#   UTF-8 and also arbitrary bytes are accepted; QuickJS treats as byte strings.
#   Use mixtures: ASCII identifiers, unicode, long identifiers, property-like strings,
#   numbers-as-strings, JSON-like, JS snippets for JS_Eval/DetectModule/ParseJSON.
# - JS_Eval/JS_EvalThis/JS_DetectModule require input[input_len] == '\0'. c_str() ensures that.
#   Provide snippets that are valid JS programs and module-like code (import/export)
#   to exercise both module detection outcomes.
# - JS_ParseJSON/JS_ParseJSON2: Provide valid JSON (objects/arrays/numbers/strings),
#   as well as edge-but-valid cases like whitespace-only, true/false/null, large numbers.
# - Property getters/setters by name: Provide typical property names including unicode,
#   dotted names, numeric indices as strings, empty name, symbols not applicable via C string.
# - js_string_codePointRange: this uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for base and for some args; supplying
#   diverse unicode including surrogate pairs and astral symbols helps.
#
# Strategy: Build a corpus of templates and choose based on seed. Ensure trailing NUL.
# Keep total size <= 4096.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

_js_programs: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "\n",  # newline only
    "42",  # numeric literal
    "'hello world'",
    "({a:1,b:2})",
    "let x=1+2; x",
    "function f(a,b){return a+b} f(3,4)",
    "class C{constructor(x){this.x=x}} new C(5).x",
    "async function g(){return 7} await g()",
    "(function(){return this})()",
    # Module-like (for JS_DetectModule true cases)
    "export const a=1;",
    "import x from 'm'; x",
    "export default 3",
    # RegExp, template string, unicode escapes
    "/a+/i.test('Aaa')",
    "`smile: 😀 length=${'😀'.length}`",
    # BigInt
    "123n + 1n",
]

_json_texts: List[str] = [
    "{}",
    "[]",
    "{\"a\":1,\"b\":true,\"c\":null}",
    "[1,2,3,4,5]",
    "\"unicode 😀\"",
    "-123.456e+7",
    "true",
    "false",
    "null",
    # whitespace-only valid JSON? No, must be a value; include value with whitespace
    " \t\n  {\"nested\": [1, {\"k\": \"v\"}], \"u\": \"😀\" }  \n",
]

_identifiers: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty property name
    "a",
    "abc",
    "_hidden",
    "$dollar",
    "with space",
    "dash-name",
    "camelCaseName",
    "PascalCase",
    "snake_case_123",
    "123",  # numeric string
    "0",
    "2147483647",
    "4294967295",
    "property.with.dots",
    "brackets[0]",
    "unicode_😀",
    "复杂属性",
    "emoji_👍_key",
]

_unicode_samples: List[str] = [
    "😀",  # U+1F600
    "𝄞",   # U+1D11E (musical symbol G clef)
    "𐍈",   # Gothic letter (astral)
    "💩",   # pile of poo
    "🏳️\u200d🌈",  # rainbow flag with ZWJ
    "कखगघङ",  # Devanagari
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "안녕하세요",  # Korean
    "مرحبا",    # Arabic
    "русский",  # Cyrillic
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢",   # Fraktur
]

_property_like: List[str] = [
    "length",
    "prototype",
    "constructor",
    "toString",
    "valueOf",
    "Symbol.toStringTag",  # not directly via string, but interesting text
    "__proto__",
    "[object Object]",
]

# Build a combined corpus to select from
_corpus: List[str] = []
_corpus.extend(_js_programs)
_corpus.extend(_json_texts)
_corpus.extend(_identifiers)
_corpus.extend(_unicode_samples)
_corpus.extend(_property_like)

# Additional generators

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix BMP and some chosen astral code points
    parts: List[str] = []
    astrals = [0x1F600, 0x1F680, 0x1F4A9, 0x1F9D1, 0x1D11E]  # 😀 🚀 💩 🧑 𝄞
    bmpranges = [
        (0x0020, 0x007E),  # printable ASCII
        (0x00A0, 0x024F),  # Latin-1 Supplement + Latin Extended-A/B
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
        (0x0600, 0x06FF),  # Arabic
        (0x3040, 0x30FF),  # Hiragana/Katakana
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),  # CJK Unified Ideographs
    ]
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            cp = rng.choice(astrals)
        else:
            lo, hi = rng.choice(bmpranges)
            cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        parts.append(chr(cp))
    return ''.join(parts)

def make_interesting_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a category
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.20:
        return rng.choice(_corpus)
    if choice < 0.35:
        # Random ASCII length 0..128
        n = rng.randint(0, 128)
        return rand_ascii(rng, n)
    if choice < 0.55:
        # Random Unicode length 0..64 code points
        n = rng.randint(0, 64)
        return rand_unicode(rng, n)
    if choice < 0.70:
        # JS snippet assembled
        parts = [rng.choice(_js_programs) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        return '\n;'.join(parts)
    if choice < 0.85:
        # JSON assembled
        parts = [rng.choice(_json_texts) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        sep = '\n' if rng.random() < 0.5 else ' '
        return sep.join(parts)
    else:
        # Property-like or identifier mixed with unicode
        base = rng.choice(_identifiers + _property_like)
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            base += '_' + rng.choice(_unicode_samples)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            base = base * rng.randint(1, 3)
        return base


def ensure_nul_terminated(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure single terminating NUL and size limit
    if data.endswith(b"\x00"):
        out = data
    else:
        out = data + b"\x00"
    # Enforce max size
    return out[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a pool of several interesting strings and pick one to return.
    # Some stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times within a single execution.
    # The harness will fetch additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR from its own RNG, but
    # providing a single strong starting buffer helps seed dictionaries/corpus.

    # Occasionally emit specific high-value samples targeting certain stubs.
    specials = [
        # Valid JS programs
        "export const a=1;",  # module detection true
        "import x from 'm'\nexport default 1",  # module
        "print('hello')",  # if std helpers present
        # Valid JSON
        "{\"a\":[1,2,3],\"b\":\"😀\"}",
        # Identifier/property
        "__proto__",
        # Unicode-heavy string for codePointRange
        "😀😀😀 𝄞𝄞 𐍈💩",
        # Very long identifier-ish string
        ("prop_" * 50) + "end",
    ]

    pick_special = rng.random() < 0.35
    if pick_special:
        s = rng.choice(specials)
    else:
        s = make_interesting_string(rng)

    # Randomly pad or combine to vary length while keeping valid C string semantics
    mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 1:
        s = s + ("\n" + make_interesting_string(rng))
    elif mode == 2:
        s = make_interesting_string(rng) + "\n" + s
    elif mode == 3:
        # Add random unicode tail
        s = s + rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(0, 16))
    # else: leave as-is

    # Truncate to keep within limit minus one for NUL
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')[:MAX_SIZE - 1]
    return ensure_nul_terminated(b)
